title: Bracket types are interchangeable
note: Round, square, and curly brackets group in exactly the same way: (a+b), [a+b] and {a+b} are identical.

title: Redundant brackets
note: Brackets around something already whole can be dropped: ((a+b)) = (a+b) = a+b, and (x) = x.

title: Brackets and order of operations
note: Multiplication happens before addition: a + b·c means a + (b·c). A bracket changes the meaning: (a+b)·c is different.

title: Implicit brackets in the fraction bar
note: The fraction bar groups the whole numerator: (a+b)/c is all of a+b over c. It is not a + b/c.

title: Minus before a bracket = ×(−1)
note: A minus in front of a bracket means multiply the whole bracket by -1: -(a+b) = (-1)(a+b) = -a-b.
